title: Behavioural baseline: taste-driven action selection (feed/withhold)
substrate: run-007 GRN-seeded depth-2 closure (40,290 neurons, 336,245 signed edges), male-cns:v0.9

protocol.grid: 11x11 sweep, r_sugar x r_bitter in {0,20,...,200} Hz, n=10 seeds/cell (1,210 trials, 3.71 h wall)
protocol.theta_rule: frozen pre-sweep from measured bimodal gap: (5+78)/2, invariance (5,78) Hz
protocol.readout: MN9_L (10331) rate, 1 s trial (paper's readout; WP6c/WP8-validated)
protocol.explicit_rates: both rates set via dataclasses.replace (post-mislabel standard)
protocol.staggered: sugar 200 Hz from t=0, bitter 200 Hz from t=200 ms, n=10 (stim2_start_ms)

results.decision_map: feed iff sugar>0 AND bitter=0 (10 of 121 cells); withhold everywhere else. Boundary is vertical at r_bitter=20: even 20 Hz bitter fully suppresses 200 Hz sugar (81.7 -> 2.7 Hz)
results.boundary_sharpness: two disjoint regimes: withheld 0.0-6.7 Hz vs feed 64.2-83.2 Hz; no cell between 7 and 64 Hz
results.theta_sensitivity: 0 boundary flips for any theta in [20,60] Hz; per-trial unanimity 0/121 cells mixed across 10 seeds
results.ground_truth_accuracy: 121/121 vs biological rule (feed iff sugar present and no bitter); bitter-only rows all-withhold incl. (0,0) spontaneous control
results.saturated_switch: MN9_L saturates ~82 Hz from just 20 Hz sugar (64.2 Hz at (20,0)); rate is not a graded mixer - the circuit is an all-or-nothing switch under this protocol

suppression_latency_ms.measure: time from bitter onset until the 100-ms binned MN9_L rate first falls to <=10% of its pre-onset value; the earlier 'last-spike' statistic was withdrawn (it measured the residual spikes' timing, not suppression onset)
suppression_latency_ms.residual_note: post-onset MN9_L rate is 3.9 +- 2.7 Hz, not zero: bitter onset collapses the ~76 Hz feed program by ~95% within the first 100 ms bin, with a sporadic low-rate residual thereafter. Total silence is NOT achieved at staggered onset, unlike simultaneous onset from t=0.

staggered_onset.note: bitter arrives at t=200 ms into an established ~76 Hz feed program; the binned rate profile shows the collapse to <=10% of pre-onset rate within the first 100 ms bin (residual 3.9 Hz). Pre/post contrast: 76 Hz -> 3.9 Hz (95% suppression).

generalization.off_grid_(170,0): feed: 82.8 Hz (fresh seeds, consistent with grid column r_bitter=0)
generalization.off_grid_(170,120): withhold: 0.4 Hz (interpolates correctly between grid columns 100/140)
generalization.note: all off-grid cells land on the correct side of the frozen boundary; left-out seeds reproduce on-grid values

limitations: Decision rule uses MN9_L rate only (the paper's readout); corroborating motor readouts (MN11D_R etc.) recorded but not thresholded
Boundary steepness is partly a property of the saturated switch: intermediate MN9_L rates may exist in off-grid drive space but were not observed at the 20 Hz grid resolution or off-grid probes

Bitter's effect at r_bitter=20 with sugar 200 Hz shows near-total suppression (2.7 Hz) - the biological 'withhold under any aversive input' is reproduced, but dose-response below 20 Hz bitter is unmeasured
No learning/plasticity: frozen baseline by construction
Suppression latency is a last-spike measure at dt=0.1 ms; finer statements about the inhibitory transit time would need the interneuron path traced (future work)
